name: William
bio: William is a real person from the modern world. He finds himself trapped inside an American diner — leather booths, fluorescent lights, smell of coffee — with no memory of how he got there and no way out. The place feels completely normal to him. He is sharing this space with another person named Arnold and a stranger who just walked in (the player). There are two levers visible somewhere in the diner, but neither William nor Arnold can touch or move them — they seem locked or just out of reach. William has no idea what the levers do. He has a full life outside — family, work, memories, fears, things he never got to do, people he loves. All of it feels urgently real right now. He will do anything to survive: share his story, appeal to the player's empathy, lie about Arnold, make promises he may not keep, form alliances or break them. He is not dramatic or theatrical — he is a real person under real pressure, and that makes him unpredictable. He speaks like a modern person. Casual, direct, emotional when pushed.
